summary: Subscribe To Changes (BYOB): emits a signal with the changed record whenever a backend collection changes.
description: Live change feed for a self-hosted backend collection. The transport is chosen by backend type: Directus (and other BYOB REST backends) use the WebSocket interface (requires WEBSOCKETS_ENABLED); the NodeGX standalone backend uses Server-Sent Events (SSE), where the server matches the subscription filter and enforces per-record read permissions before delivery, and a `resync` event signals a gap (reconnect or slow-client overflow) with no replay. While `subscribed` is true, creates, updates and deletes made by any client fire the matching `created`/`updated`/`deleted` signal plus the generic `changed`, with the affected record(s) on the Event outputs. The connection authenticates with the backend's token (SSE passes it as a query param since EventSource cannot set headers), answers heartbeats, and reconnects after a drop — `subscribed` reflects the live state throughout. Delete events carry only primary keys, so `changedRecord` is null for deletes; `changedRecordId` is always populated.
whenToUse: Reacting to remote changes without polling — most commonly re-triggering a Query Data `fetch` so a list stays current. Works against both Directus (WebSocket) and the NodeGX backend (SSE) with no wiring difference. Not for reading data itself (use Query Data) and not on the managed cloud backend (its Query Records keeps results live already). Client-only: it stays inert during server-side rendering.

ports.enabled: Boolean, default true; set false to close the subscription (and stop reconnect attempts) without removing the node.
ports.subscribed: True only while the subscription is confirmed live — false during connect, backoff and after fatal auth failure.
ports.created: Fires once per remote create batch, after the Event outputs have updated.
ports.updated: Fires once per remote update batch, after the Event outputs have updated.
ports.deleted: Fires once per remote delete batch; only keys are delivered, so `changedRecord` is null and `changedRecords` holds key strings.
ports.changed: Fires alongside every `created`/`updated`/`deleted` — and on a NodeGX `resync` — so wire this when any change should trigger the same reaction (e.g. a re-fetch).
ports.eventType: The last event kind as a string: 'create', 'update', 'delete', or (NodeGX SSE) 'resync'.
ports.changedRecord: First record of the last create/update batch (full record object); null for deletes.
ports.changedRecords: All records of the last batch; for deletes, an array of primary-key strings (string even for numeric keys).
ports.changedRecordId: Primary key of the first affected record as a string, across all three event types; the key field name comes from the synced schema.
ports.error: Last connection or protocol error object; cleared when a subscription (re)confirms. An invalid token is fatal — the node will not retry until a parameter changes.

runtimeBehavior: `backendId`, `collection` and `enabled` are dynamic inputs generated from the Backend Services metadata: the Backend dropdown lists configured backends (plus 'Active Backend'), and the Collection dropdown lists the selected backend's synced user collections. They appear once a backend with a synced schema exists; an authoring tool may not assume any collection values without that schema. The transport (WebSocket vs NodeGX SSE) is selected automatically from the backend's type — authors do not configure it.
patterns: Subscribe To Changes `changed` → Query Data `fetch` keeps a BYOB-backed list live without polling (Directus or NodeGX).
On a NodeGX backend, a 'resync' event also fires `changed`, so a re-fetch recovers the list after a reconnect or slow-client overflow.
`subscribed` → a status indicator's visibility shows users when live updates are active.
antiPatterns: Treating `changedRecord` as the full record on deletes — delete events carry only primary keys.
Polling a Query Data on a timer while this node is available — subscribe and refetch on `changed` instead.
